kernel.name: lazy_curveball_uniform_trade
kernel.transition: hold with probability 1/2; otherwise choose an unordered row pair uniformly and choose a subset of the symmetric difference uniformly with the first row's original unique-neighbor cardinality
kernel.stationary_target: uniform over all simple bipartite matrices with the exact observed row and column degrees
kernel.detailed_balance_reason: The selected row-pair symmetric difference is invariant under reversal, and the subset cardinality is fixed by the first row degree; forward and reverse allocations have equal probability.
kernel.irreducibility_reason: Every valid 2-switch is a possible one-neighbor Curveball trade; the bipartite 2-switch graph connects all realizations of a graphical degree sequence.

theorem_2.reference: Erdos et al. 2018, PLOS ONE 13(8), e0201995, Theorem 2

kernel_rate_comparison.reference_kernel: Erdos et al. 2018 Theorem 2/3 chain: lazy half-hold, then uniform choice of a row-pair and column-pair
kernel_rate_comparison.implemented_kernel: lazy half-hold, then uniform choice of two distinct edge slots
kernel_rate_comparison.scope: For each valid 2-switch the move probabilities are state-independent constants; the kernels differ by a scalar factor on off-diagonal moves and a compensating self-loop. This reports the discrete-time rate comparison; it does not itself certify mixing for a sequence outside the theorem hypotheses.

theorem_3.reference: Erdos et al. 2018, PLOS ONE 13(8), e0201995, Theorem 3

theory_screen.interpretation: No screened sufficient theorem certifies rapid mixing for this degree sequence. This does NOT establish slow mixing; empirical convergence diagnostics and/or other theory remain necessary.

mixing_diagnostics.warning: These finite-chain diagnostics do not prove stationarity, rapid mixing, or a calibrated test.

distance_distribution_stability.warning: A stable distance distribution is not proof of stationarity; the distance statistic may stabilize before other graph features mix. D is an effect size only; serial dependence is not converted into an iid KS p-value.

inference.reason: Curveball is an alternative uniform-stationary kernel; finite-run convergence is not established by kernel validity or distance stabilization alone.
